question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to \,-4}\frac{{y}^{2}+y-12}{{y}^{2}+4y} & =\frac{(-4)^{2}+(-4)-12}{(-4)^{2}+4(-4)}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}+y-12}{{y}^{2}+4y} & =\frac{(y+4)(y-3)}{y(y+4)} \\  & =\frac{y-3}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to \,-4}\frac{{y}^{2}+y-12}{{y}^{2}+4y} & ={lim}_{y\to \,-4}\frac{y-3}{y} \\  & =\frac{-4-3}{-4} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
